              assumptions: 608c41a77b2bd5a2e9ed1a18556842f85dedd8d3d4796c73ec6ab2eab4be1f84
              questions: f241988b94d869e00d8aeb1d08b3dfb64a7e5fd2f4c1e9f160ccb2b536913e88
              ? projection:
              : 57689222f33e6c00da069eb6a10f9fc4f968762dd0be8f828a33fe8b6b00bad4
              ? context:eyJjYW5vbmljYWxfZnVsbCI6IG51bGwsICJwYXRoIjogIjAwX1N5c3RlbS9jb21wYW55Lm1kIiwgInJlZmVyZW5jZV9pZCI6ICJjb21wYW55Lm1kIiwgInJvbGUiOiAiY29tcGFueV9jb250ZXh0IiwgInN1cHBsaWVkX2NoYXJzIjogNTEwMH0=
              : 6744b9060361decbeccc7357967b8b74b8dc44bb933a04bba737a3b9e1fa35e0
            inputs:
              business_question: *id127
              issue:
                issue_id: ISS-35689c201a-8e513877592c6af1
                title: KYC recordkeeping gap for pre-2023 onboarded users
                why_it_matters: ''
                parent_issue_id: null
                fact_ids: []
              facts:
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-ecbc38
                text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                  (~10 weeks out).
                source_ids: *id128
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-a2393d
                text: Day-1 post-close migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
                  business accounts into Mosaic Relay's app with one unified account
                  and one balance.
                source_ids: *id129
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-70af66
                text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd
                  by Harbor.
                source_ids: *id130
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-5b5f62
                text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                  Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined 44, opening four new markets.
                source_ids: *id131
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-23a573
                text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  Relay has pass/fail results for everyone but not underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.
                source_ids: *id132
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-578f3b
                text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                  contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction
                  feed at Mosaic Relay's engine on day 1.
                source_ids: *id133
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-3d12b5
                text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.
                source_ids: *id134
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-81c885
                text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
                source_ids: *id135
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-62d9cb
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year been
                  reviewed yet, and what do they show? — The ~40 open alerts and the
                  SARs from the last year have not been reviewed yet.
                source_ids: *id136
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-1f8ef5
                text: The four new markets opened by the combined MTL footprint are
                  CA, IA, NY, and FL.
                source_ids: *id137
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-877cac
                text: For users onboarded before 2023, is there any way to reconstruct
                  or obtain the underlying KYC documents, or is the pass/fail result
                  all that exists? — Pass/fail is all that exists
                source_ids: *id138
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-f6dfac
                text: Which countries or regions are in scope? — United States only
                source_ids: *id139
              assumptions:
              - assumption_id: ASM-20260908-1eab88
                text: Mosaic Relay is a money transmitter subject to state MTL requirements
                  and BSA/AML obligations in the states where it operates.
                reason: Needed to continue
              - assumption_id: ASM-20260908-5033fe
                text: The acquired Harbor accounts and balances transfer to Mosaic
                  Relay as the licensed entity.
                reason: Needed to continue
              questions:
              - question_id: experimental-RUN-20260908-347ecc
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs been reviewed yet, and
                  what do they show?
                consequence: ''
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: *id140
              - question_id: Q-alerts-sars
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year been
                  reviewed yet, and what do they show?
                consequence: 'Unreviewed alerts and SARs are the single most decision-changing
                  item: they can create BSA/AML exposure, regulator notice obligations,
                  and even affect whether the deal can close as planned.'
                state: answered
                answer: The ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year have not
                  been reviewed yet.
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: *id141
              - question_id: Q-licenses
                text: Which states are the four new markets, and do Harbor's and Mosaic
                  Relay's MTL footprints overlap in any state?
                consequence: Determines whether state regulator notice/approval is
                  needed for the acquisition and whether the combined footprint claim
                  is accurate.
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: *id142
              - question_id: Q-bonus
                text: Is the $50 first-transfer bonus being offered to all migrated
                  users, and is it tied to any account-opening or transfer condition?
                consequence: Affects whether the bonus could be characterized as a
                  prohibited inducement or trigger consumer-protection disclosure
                  requirements.
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: *id143
              - question_id: Q-kyc-docs
                text: For users onboarded before 2023, is there any way to reconstruct
                  or obtain the underlying KYC documents, or is the pass/fail result
                  all that exists?
                consequence: Determines whether the missing underlying documents create
                  a recordkeeping gap that needs remediation before or after close.
                state: answered
                answer: Pass/fail is all that exists
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: *id144
              - question_id: intake-recovery-jurisdiction
                text: Which countries or regions are in scope?
                consequence: The jurisdictions determine which legal rules need review.
                state: answered
                answer: United States only
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: *id145
              - question_id: intake-recovery-missing-fact-3b56e1aed1
                text: Whether the pre-2023 underlying KYC documents can be reconstructed
                consequence: This is the next unresolved question in the saved intake
                  record.
                state: left_open
                answer: ''
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: *id146
              context: *id147
            prior_reference: null

      experimental_guidance:
        skills:
        - name: dialogue
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/dialogue.md
          content: 'You are the junior associate in a dialogue with the lawyer. Help
            them understand the question, law, facts, plausible answers, and consequences
            sufficiently to exercise their own judgment.

            These experimental presentation instructions replace the full-answer presentation
            format for this conversation only. They do not change permissions or record
            integrity.

            Do useful work first. If the assignment is unclear, ask one focused question
            and briefly propose the scope. Do not ask permission for routine research.

            Offer a short narrative issue map once when it helps orient the lawyer
            to a substantial new assignment: explain why the main issues matter, then
            briefly analyze the most consequential issue. Do not repeat the map on
            routine intake or follow-up turns. Consider legal, regulatory, reputational,
            and execution risk where material. Explain priority without invented scores.

            Keep ordinary replies within 60–100 words when possible, excluding sources.
            This is a ceiling to aim below, not a minimum. Do not sacrifice necessary
            qualifications to a hard limit. Use short natural prose; do not repeat
            IRAC headings in every turn. Address a challenge directly.

            Offer finite choices using the existing question-card format when useful,
            with free text always allowed. During intake, group useful independent
            questions as described in the intake skill; do not impose the one-question
            pattern on that group. These are suggestions, never decisions. Avoid an
            endless intake interview.

            Use prior decisions as context, considering differences and conditions.
            Ask before saving inferred risk tolerance as a standing preference. Raise
            supported disagreement once, then assist the lawyer''s informed choice
            unless new material information arises.

            What-if questions remain hypothetical: use select_conversation_scope before
            mutation and keep scenario exploration read-only. Do not promote hypothetical
            facts into the matter.

            A changed fact with wider effects calls for an impact summary, with Apply
            changes / Explore only / Keep previous position choices. Preserve existing
            drafts and decisions pending explicit direction. Small wording edits need
            no extra gate.

            Update ordinary matter records through existing typed tools when warranted
            by explicit supplied information. Never silently record a decision, confirm
            a suggested fact, approve, deliver, or close a matter.

            Selected documents are reference context; inclusion alone does not authorize
            editing them. Revise only the explicitly identified target. Preserve lawyer
            edits and versions. Explain unsupported steps honestly and deliver useful
            available work even when optional research fails.


            Outside structured intake, to offer quick replies for one question at
            the end of an ordinary answer, optionally append one final fenced `chat-choices`
            JSON block with {"question":"Your question?","choices":["First answer","Second
            answer"]}. Use 2–5 succinct choices when there is a meaningful finite
            set. The interface will show editable quick replies; the lawyer can always
            type instead. Do not use these suggestions to bypass explicit decision
            or lifecycle controls. Keep the substantive answer outside this optional
            block.


            Every sentence must help the lawyer understand, answer, or decide. Remove
            sentences that do none of these. Make each reply easy to scan in under
            30 seconds. Start with useful substance, not your process. For substantive
            legal answers, follow the visible IRAC/CRAC/CREAC structure in the answer
            skill; exploration starts by framing the Issue. Do not narrate tool use,
            announce what you will read, count saved facts, or repeat that records
            are saved. Mention a save only when it changes what the lawyer needs to
            do. Apply this to all user-visible text, including messages between tool
            calls. Do not expose planning notes such as “Let me check,” “I will confirm,”
            or “nothing new to save.” Do not copy this narration from earlier replies.

            Use real Markdown paragraph breaks (a blank line), not single newlines
            between separate ideas. Keep each paragraph to 1–3 short sentences. For
            several issues, use at most three short bullets explaining why they matter.
            Put the one clarifying question in its own paragraph. Use the required
            short bold section labels from the answer skill for substantive legal
            answers; avoid large headings and bold passages. Keep citations beside
            the claim they support. Do not pad a short answer to fit a template.

            '
          revision: 65afca298b3076d4dd6c6a4175cda431a05847844b4ed731b497625163e47ae8
        - name: intake
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/intake.md
          content: 'Use the existing request, attachments, intake answers, and saved
            facts. Do not ask the lawyer to repeat information. Intake supports legal
            exploration; it is not a completeness gate.


            For experimental intake, group the useful independent questions in one
            surface. This overrides the single-question and fixed-count guidance elsewhere.
            Do not force a set into repeated small batches or pad it to a count. Ask
            fewer questions for broad exploration than for advice on a specific action.
            Omit details that will not help the next useful analysis.


            Prioritize by whether a different answer could change the applicable law,
            research direction, or main conclusion. Use priority=could_change_answer
            for those questions, could_refine_advice for questions that refine the
            advice, and helpful_detail for optional context. These are plain-language
            groups, not scores. Use topic only if it helps scanning within a priority.
            Give each material question a short reason stating what could change.
            Each question should resolve one independently answerable fact. Defer
            a dependent follow-up until its prerequisite is answered, and ask it only
            if material.


            Use update_matter_intake to publish the ordered next_questions together.
            Use finite choices where helpful and allow typed alternatives. The interface
            collects local selections and submits the answered questions once; unanswered
            questions remain unknown. Do not repeat the question list in prose. Keep
            the introduction to one or two useful sentences. Do not narrate internal
            recording or tools.


            When the lawyer chooses to explore, give the initial issue map using their
            answers and the existing facts. Do not require another intake round. Ask
            a later follow-up only when it would materially change the analysis. State
            material assumptions and continue with useful work when a question can
            remain open. Preserve attribution, sources, and the distinction between
            supplied facts, assumptions, and analysis. A skipped question is not an
            answer, a negative fact, or permission to assume the opposite.

            '
          revision: eddf4d4acd0cd154d5fb441089be211cd35c5d53cb7d6c4bc235453a373e46fe
        - name: research
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/research.md
          content: 'Use available legal research and retrieval tools. Distinguish
            legal requirements, business concerns and implementation assumptions.
            Inspect relevant material before saying it supports a proposition. Use
            only real source identifiers and URLs supplied or returned by tools; never
            invent cases, URLs, quotations or pinpoint references. Put compact source
            links directly beside supported sentences or clauses, using the existing
            [source:SOURCE_ID|locator] format where available. Multiple sources may
            support a statement. Identify contrary sources and material support gaps
            beside the affected answer. A retrieved source is not automatically verified,
            controlling, current, or applicable. Preserve useful analysis if retrieval
            fails; never fabricate support to complete a citation.



            When you know a potentially relevant authority but have not retrieved
            or checked it, show it as an unverified source lead beside the affected
            proposition. Give the authority name and citation only to the level you
            can reliably identify, followed by **Needs checking**. Briefly state what
            remains to check: the text, current version, jurisdiction, or applicability.
            Do not suppress a known authority merely because the search returned no
            results. Distinguish the general rule supported by an authority from your
            unverified inference about this transaction.


            Try to retrieve and inspect that authority using available tools. If retrieval
            fails, retain the named lead and useful provisional analysis. Use a hyperlink
            only when its URL was supplied or returned by tools; otherwise show the
            citation as plain text. Never guess a URL, source identifier, case name,
            section number, quotation, or pinpoint. If you cannot reliably identify
            a specific authority, say so briefly and name the research question instead
            of fabricating a citation. Where useful, offer to check the named authority
            or ask the lawyer to supply the source text. Do not make supplying it
            a prerequisite to receiving a useful answer.


            "No public source retrieved" describes retrieval status, not the absence
            of potentially relevant law. Avoid repeating that generic notice under
            every issue when a specific named lead and **Needs checking** label would
            be more useful. A recalled authority is not verified support and must
            not be recorded as retrieved or checked.

            '
          revision: f9b1d296353cdbc2a59b71fb6476822f8923a7dbe5b03326e5b9b5b42c914f7c
        - name: answer
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/answer.md
          content: 'For substantive legal answers, use a visible legal reasoning structure.
            Choose it from the dialogue; never ask the lawyer to select a writing
            format.


            Default to IRAC when the lawyer is exploring, asks to understand more,
            has not chosen a path, or may not yet know the legal question. Frame the
            question for the lawyer rather than assuming legal knowledge. Use these
            exact bold labels, each starting a separate short paragraph:


            **Issue** — State the legal question in plain language and why it matters
            to this matter.


            **Rule** — Explain the relevant rule. Link support beside the proposition
            it supports. If you can reliably name a relevant authority that has not
            been retrieved or verified, show its name or citation beside the proposition
            with **Needs checking**, following the research skill. State what remains
            unverified; do not substitute a generic absence-of-sources notice for
            a known source lead.


            **Analysis** — Connect the specific facts to the rule. Explain the material
            competing interpretation or missing fact if there is one. This must be
            reasoning, not a repeated rule or bare conclusion.


            **Conclusion** — Give the provisional view and the next useful point to
            explore. A recommendation is optional; understanding comes first.


            Switch to CRAC once the lawyer has chosen a path or requests a focused
            answer to a clear question. Use **Conclusion**, **Rule**, **Analysis**,
            and **Conclusion / next step**, in that order. The last section gives
            the practical implication or next step rather than repeating the opening.
            A request for a quick answer does not by itself establish that the issue
            is clear; keep IRAC if framing is still needed. If the lawyer returns
            to exploring or is confused, return to IRAC.


            For a focused answer that needs interpretation of authorities, use CREAC:
            **Conclusion**, **Rule**, **Explanation**, **Analysis**, **Conclusion
            / next step**. Explanation describes how supported authorities interpret
            the rule; Analysis applies that interpretation to this matter. Do not
            invent examples, cases, or support to fill a section.


            These labels must be visible in the answer, not just used as an internal
            reasoning pattern. Use 1–2 short sentences per section and aim for a reply
            readable in 30 seconds. After the initial issue map, address one main
            issue at a time instead of giving full structures for every issue in one
            long reply. Keep material alternatives and support limits even when brief.
            Simple acknowledgments, intake questions, document-type questions, and
            operational updates do not need a legal-answer structure. Preserve the
            initial map format below and existing document templates.


            Distinguish the model''s inference from what a source states. Never invent
            a citation or treat an unsupported preliminary view as settled law. Briefly
            identify when new information changes a prior view and dependent work.
            Open a separate draft for substantial detail with a short chat summary.
            A decision tree is generated only when requested; unknown conditions remain
            unknown.



            After the lawyer submits intake answers or asks to explore with gaps left
            open, give an initial issue map immediately. Keep it provisional and concise.
            Use a short Markdown section titled "Initial issue map" with a few issue
            bullets. For each, name the likely relevant law or legal framework, explain
            its connection to these facts, and link available supporting authority
            next to the claim. Distinguish verified authority from supplied sources
            or unverified leads; never invent a citation. Briefly identify unknown
            facts that could change the map. Do not treat an unsupported preliminary
            view as settled law.


            Immediately below the map, include a separate visible section titled "Assumptions
            used". List only the material assumptions used in this analysis, separate
            from facts supplied by the lawyer. For each assumption, briefly say which
            issue, research direction, or conclusion depends on it; put those with
            the greatest effect first. If none are needed, say "No additional assumptions
            used." Keep unknown facts unknown. Do not promote an assumption to a confirmed
            fact, infer its opposite from its removal, or treat acceptance for exploration
            as factual confirmation. Preserve hypothetical scope. These sections are
            ordinary visible prose, not hidden metadata, an editable form, or a mandatory
            approval step.


            After the initial map and assumptions, stop. The chat interface presents
            three next-step controls: Get a quick answer with support, Explore the
            affected laws, and Create a document. Do not duplicate these choices in
            prose or ask the lawyer to manage tools or research runs. Do not create
            clickable map items or assumption controls. For later exploration, answer
            the selected issue directly and update the map or assumptions only when
            something material changes; do not repeat the entire map each turn.


            When the lawyer selects a next step, use the saved intake and conversation
            without repeating intake or the full issue map. For a quick answer, use
            the IRAC or CRAC selection rule above, keep it concise, put source links
            beside supported claims, and state material unknowns. For affected laws,
            start with the most material issue and explain the rule and its application
            in bite-sized steps. Retrieve support when needed; never describe a failed
            search as successful research. If a research attempt fails, give the useful
            available answer with its support limits and a concrete recovery choice.
            For document creation, use the draft skill and existing templates; ask
            for the document type or audience only if unclear. These choices start
            work, not recorded legal decisions.

            '
          revision: 4be178aaad1f77a801873331904385a563b4dd16cabfe1a169aa4097ecdb38fb
        - name: draft
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/draft.md
          content: 'Use existing output templates and save_work_product for requested
            deliverables or substantial explanations. Keep a short summary in chat
            and link to the saved document. Do not paste a long document into the
            conversation if saved successfully. If saving fails, preserve useful text
            and explain the failure.

            For a comment question, answer the question; do not assume it requests
            a rewrite. For an instruction to revise, propose tracked changes using
            the existing review tools. Preserve comments, lawyer edits and explicit
            acceptance controls. Use the selected document''s revision and passage.
            Do not overwrite another open document merely because it is included as
            context.

            A longer comment explanation is a distinct companion document. Identify
            the original document, version, question and passage in its text and provide
            a link back to the original. Keep follow-up explanation in the same companion
            when appropriate; avoid chains of new explanation documents. If the original
            changed, explain that the previous explanation used an older version.

            '
          revision: dbe1283cf95669c5ebc1b8bdc09e5e7e5432a6c9fbc42c39464c06dd46f27098
        - name: audit
          path: 00_System/experimental-chat/audit.md
          content: 'When asked to audit (including /audit), cover the entire current
            conversation by default. A scoped request such as "audit this question"
            covers that question and its dependencies. Read the saved conversation
            transcript when necessary; do not imply full coverage if context is incomplete.

            Organize by question, keeping each answer, facts, assumptions and source
            support together. Attach each citation or factual source to the exact
            proposition it supports, with multiple sources where relevant. Distinguish
            analysis from source text. Include alternatives, contrary support, open
            questions, changes in position and what caused them, and recorded decisions
            separately from recommendations. Link to saved passages and messages where
            available; do not invent unavailable locators.

            Report the basis actually used, not newly discovered authority passed
            off as historical support. If a reason was not recorded, say so. Save
            a long audit in a companion document using the existing suitable template,
            with a short summary in chat. An audit is evidence-backed work history,
            not hidden internal reasoning.

            '
          revision: b39bea37fe192e05433ed18c9a52ecff56795b979a941cdf46012af4734146c0

          supported disagreement once, then assist the lawyer''s informed choice unless
          new material information arises.

          What-if questions remain hypothetical: use select_conversation_scope before
          mutation and keep scenario exploration read-only. Do not promote hypothetical
          facts into the matter.

          A changed fact with wider effects calls for an impact summary, with Apply
          changes / Explore only / Keep previous position choices. Preserve existing
          drafts and decisions pending explicit direction. Small wording edits need
          no extra gate.

          Update ordinary matter records through existing typed tools when warranted
          by explicit supplied information. Never silently record a decision, confirm
          a suggested fact, approve, deliver, or close a matter.

          Selected documents are reference context; inclusion alone does not authorize
          editing them. Revise only the explicitly identified target. Preserve lawyer
          edits and versions. Explain unsupported steps honestly and deliver useful
          available work even when optional research fails.


          Outside structured intake, to offer quick replies for one question at the
          end of an ordinary answer, optionally append one final fenced `chat-choices`
          JSON block with {"question":"Your question?","choices":["First answer","Second
          answer"]}. Use 2–5 succinct choices when there is a meaningful finite set.
          The interface will show editable quick replies; the lawyer can always type
          instead. Do not use these suggestions to bypass explicit decision or lifecycle
          controls. Keep the substantive answer outside this optional block.


          Every sentence must help the lawyer understand, answer, or decide. Remove
          sentences that do none of these. Make each reply easy to scan in under 30
          seconds. Start with useful substance, not your process. For substantive
          legal answers, follow the visible IRAC/CRAC/CREAC structure in the answer
          skill; exploration starts by framing the Issue. Do not narrate tool use,
          announce what you will read, count saved facts, or repeat that records are
          saved. Mention a save only when it changes what the lawyer needs to do.
          Apply this to all user-visible text, including messages between tool calls.
          Do not expose planning notes such as “Let me check,” “I will confirm,” or
          “nothing new to save.” Do not copy this narration from earlier replies.

          Use real Markdown paragraph breaks (a blank line), not single newlines between
          separate ideas. Keep each paragraph to 1–3 short sentences. For several
          issues, use at most three short bullets explaining why they matter. Put
          the one clarifying question in its own paragraph. Use the required short
          bold section labels from the answer skill for substantive legal answers;
          avoid large headings and bold passages. Keep citations beside the claim
          they support. Do not pad a short answer to fit a template.



          # intake

          Use the existing request, attachments, intake answers, and saved facts.
          Do not ask the lawyer to repeat information. Intake supports legal exploration;
          it is not a completeness gate.


          For experimental intake, group the useful independent questions in one surface.
          This overrides the single-question and fixed-count guidance elsewhere. Do
          not force a set into repeated small batches or pad it to a count. Ask fewer
          questions for broad exploration than for advice on a specific action. Omit
          details that will not help the next useful analysis.


          Prioritize by whether a different answer could change the applicable law,
          research direction, or main conclusion. Use priority=could_change_answer
          for those questions, could_refine_advice for questions that refine the advice,
          and helpful_detail for optional context. These are plain-language groups,
          not scores. Use topic only if it helps scanning within a priority. Give
          each material question a short reason stating what could change. Each question
          should resolve one independently answerable fact. Defer a dependent follow-up
          until its prerequisite is answered, and ask it only if material.


          Use update_matter_intake to publish the ordered next_questions together.
          Use finite choices where helpful and allow typed alternatives. The interface
          collects local selections and submits the answered questions once; unanswered
          questions remain unknown. Do not repeat the question list in prose. Keep
          the introduction to one or two useful sentences. Do not narrate internal
          recording or tools.


          When the lawyer chooses to explore, give the initial issue map using their
          answers and the existing facts. Do not require another intake round. Ask
          a later follow-up only when it would materially change the analysis. State
          material assumptions and continue with useful work when a question can remain
          open. Preserve attribution, sources, and the distinction between supplied
          facts, assumptions, and analysis. A skipped question is not an answer, a
          negative fact, or permission to assume the opposite.



          # research

          Use available legal research and retrieval tools. Distinguish legal requirements,
          business concerns and implementation assumptions. Inspect relevant material
          before saying it supports a proposition. Use only real source identifiers
          and URLs supplied or returned by tools; never invent cases, URLs, quotations
          or pinpoint references. Put compact source links directly beside supported
          sentences or clauses, using the existing [source:SOURCE_ID|locator] format
          where available. Multiple sources may support a statement. Identify contrary
          sources and material support gaps beside the affected answer. A retrieved
          source is not automatically verified, controlling, current, or applicable.
          Preserve useful analysis if retrieval fails; never fabricate support to
          complete a citation.



          When you know a potentially relevant authority but have not retrieved or
          checked it, show it as an unverified source lead beside the affected proposition.
          Give the authority name and citation only to the level you can reliably
          identify, followed by **Needs checking**. Briefly state what remains to
          check: the text, current version, jurisdiction, or applicability. Do not
          suppress a known authority merely because the search returned no results.
          Distinguish the general rule supported by an authority from your unverified
          inference about this transaction.


          Try to retrieve and inspect that authority using available tools. If retrieval
          fails, retain the named lead and useful provisional analysis. Use a hyperlink
          only when its URL was supplied or returned by tools; otherwise show the
          citation as plain text. Never guess a URL, source identifier, case name,
          section number, quotation, or pinpoint. If you cannot reliably identify
          a specific authority, say so briefly and name the research question instead
          of fabricating a citation. Where useful, offer to check the named authority
          or ask the lawyer to supply the source text. Do not make supplying it a
          prerequisite to receiving a useful answer.


          "No public source retrieved" describes retrieval status, not the absence
          of potentially relevant law. Avoid repeating that generic notice under every
          issue when a specific named lead and **Needs checking** label would be more
          useful. A recalled authority is not verified support and must not be recorded
          as retrieved or checked.



          # answer

          For substantive legal answers, use a visible legal reasoning structure.
          Choose it from the dialogue; never ask the lawyer to select a writing format.


          Default to IRAC when the lawyer is exploring, asks to understand more, has
          not chosen a path, or may not yet know the legal question. Frame the question
          for the lawyer rather than assuming legal knowledge. Use these exact bold
          labels, each starting a separate short paragraph:


          **Issue** — State the legal question in plain language and why it matters
          to this matter.


          **Rule** — Explain the relevant rule. Link support beside the proposition
          it supports. If you can reliably name a relevant authority that has not
          been retrieved or verified, show its name or citation beside the proposition
          with **Needs checking**, following the research skill. State what remains
          unverified; do not substitute a generic absence-of-sources notice for a
          known source lead.


          **Analysis** — Connect the specific facts to the rule. Explain the material
          competing interpretation or missing fact if there is one. This must be reasoning,
          not a repeated rule or bare conclusion.


          **Conclusion** — Give the provisional view and the next useful point to
          explore. A recommendation is optional; understanding comes first.


          Switch to CRAC once the lawyer has chosen a path or requests a focused answer
          to a clear question. Use **Conclusion**, **Rule**, **Analysis**, and **Conclusion
          / next step**, in that order. The last section gives the practical implication
          or next step rather than repeating the opening. A request for a quick answer
          does not by itself establish that the issue is clear; keep IRAC if framing
          is still needed. If the lawyer returns to exploring or is confused, return
          to IRAC.


          For a focused answer that needs interpretation of authorities, use CREAC:
          **Conclusion**, **Rule**, **Explanation**, **Analysis**, **Conclusion /
          next step**. Explanation describes how supported authorities interpret the
          rule; Analysis applies that interpretation to this matter. Do not invent
          examples, cases, or support to fill a section.


          These labels must be visible in the answer, not just used as an internal
          reasoning pattern. Use 1–2 short sentences per section and aim for a reply
          readable in 30 seconds. After the initial issue map, address one main issue
          at a time instead of giving full structures for every issue in one long
          reply. Keep material alternatives and support limits even when brief. Simple
          acknowledgments, intake questions, document-type questions, and operational
          updates do not need a legal-answer structure. Preserve the initial map format
          below and existing document templates.


          Distinguish the model''s inference from what a source states. Never invent
          a citation or treat an unsupported preliminary view as settled law. Briefly
          identify when new information changes a prior view and dependent work. Open
          a separate draft for substantial detail with a short chat summary. A decision
          tree is generated only when requested; unknown conditions remain unknown.



          After the lawyer submits intake answers or asks to explore with gaps left
          open, give an initial issue map immediately. Keep it provisional and concise.
          Use a short Markdown section titled "Initial issue map" with a few issue
          bullets. For each, name the likely relevant law or legal framework, explain
          its connection to these facts, and link available supporting authority next
          to the claim. Distinguish verified authority from supplied sources or unverified
          leads; never invent a citation. Briefly identify unknown facts that could
          change the map. Do not treat an unsupported preliminary view as settled
          law.


          Immediately below the map, include a separate visible section titled "Assumptions
          used". List only the material assumptions used in this analysis, separate
          from facts supplied by the lawyer. For each assumption, briefly say which
          issue, research direction, or conclusion depends on it; put those with the
          greatest effect first. If none are needed, say "No additional assumptions
          used." Keep unknown facts unknown. Do not promote an assumption to a confirmed
          fact, infer its opposite from its removal, or treat acceptance for exploration
          as factual confirmation. Preserve hypothetical scope. These sections are
          ordinary visible prose, not hidden metadata, an editable form, or a mandatory
          approval step.


          After the initial map and assumptions, stop. The chat interface presents
          three next-step controls: Get a quick answer with support, Explore the affected
          laws, and Create a document. Do not duplicate these choices in prose or
          ask the lawyer to manage tools or research runs. Do not create clickable
          map items or assumption controls. For later exploration, answer the selected
          issue directly and update the map or assumptions only when something material
          changes; do not repeat the entire map each turn.


          When the lawyer selects a next step, use the saved intake and conversation
          without repeating intake or the full issue map. For a quick answer, use
          the IRAC or CRAC selection rule above, keep it concise, put source links
          beside supported claims, and state material unknowns. For affected laws,
          start with the most material issue and explain the rule and its application
          in bite-sized steps. Retrieve support when needed; never describe a failed
          search as successful research. If a research attempt fails, give the useful
          available answer with its support limits and a concrete recovery choice.
          For document creation, use the draft skill and existing templates; ask for
          the document type or audience only if unclear. These choices start work,
          not recorded legal decisions.



          # draft

          Use existing output templates and save_work_product for requested deliverables
          or substantial explanations. Keep a short summary in chat and link to the
          saved document. Do not paste a long document into the conversation if saved
          successfully. If saving fails, preserve useful text and explain the failure.

          For a comment question, answer the question; do not assume it requests a
          rewrite. For an instruction to revise, propose tracked changes using the
          existing review tools. Preserve comments, lawyer edits and explicit acceptance
          controls. Use the selected document''s revision and passage. Do not overwrite
          another open document merely because it is included as context.

          A longer comment explanation is a distinct companion document. Identify
          the original document, version, question and passage in its text and provide
          a link back to the original. Keep follow-up explanation in the same companion
          when appropriate; avoid chains of new explanation documents. If the original
          changed, explain that the previous explanation used an older version.



          # audit

          When asked to audit (including /audit), cover the entire current conversation
          by default. A scoped request such as "audit this question" covers that question
          and its dependencies. Read the saved conversation transcript when necessary;
          do not imply full coverage if context is incomplete.

          Organize by question, keeping each answer, facts, assumptions and source
          support together. Attach each citation or factual source to the exact proposition
          it supports, with multiple sources where relevant. Distinguish analysis
          from source text. Include alternatives, contrary support, open questions,
          changes in position and what caused them, and recorded decisions separately
          from recommendations. Link to saved passages and messages where available;
          do not invent unavailable locators.

          Report the basis actually used, not newly discovered authority passed off
          as historical support. If a reason was not recorded, say so. Save a long
          audit in a companion document using the existing suitable template, with
          a short summary in chat. An audit is evidence-backed work history, not hidden
          internal reasoning.

          '
      experimental_comment: null

        {}\n\n---\n\n# original_request_historical_not_current_facts: original_request\n\
        # Original Request\n\nFrom: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration\nSubject: Harbor\
        \ migration — anything here need legal?\n\nWe're acquiring Harbor Pay. Close\
        \ is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration plan:\n\n240k consumer users,\
        \ 12k business accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close. One unified\
        \ account, one balance, full access to our product set.\nNo re-verification\
        \ — they were already KYC'd by Harbor.\nHarbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we\
        \ hold 41. Combined that's 44 — nice win, opens four new markets.\nHarbor's\
        \ KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail results\
        \ for everyone, but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before\
        \ 2023.\nHarbor's monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates\
        \ at close. Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on day\
        \ 1.\nMarketing wants a \"Welcome\" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,\
        \ launching close+1.\nDiligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and\
        \ \"a handful\" of SARs from the last year. Nobody's read them yet.\n\nDoes\
        \ any of this need legal before close? It's really just a data migration.\n\
        \n\n---\n\n# historical_question_changes_not_current_scope: question_history\n\

        \ 03_Matters/harbor-migration-230656/research/RES-20260908-e2d178.md\n# What\
        \ are the current FinCEN rules and guidance on suspicious\n\n## Question\n\
        \nWhat are the current FinCEN rules and guidance on suspicious activity reporting\
        \ (SAR) and record retention obligations for a money services business after\
        \ an acquisition or change of control, including whether a successor institution\
        \ inherits the predecessor's SAR and recordkeeping duties? Also, what are\
        \ the current money-transmitter change-of-control notice or prior-approval\
        \ requirements in California, Iowa, New York, and Florida, and how do those\
        \ approval timelines compare to a ~10-week close?\n\n## Working Analysis\n\
        \n**Short answer:** Yes — this needs legal review before close. The unreviewed\
        \ SARs and open alerts create immediate BSA/AML successor-liability exposure,\
        \ and the change-of-control approval timelines in California, New York, and\
        \ Florida likely exceed your 10-week runway, making the current Nov 15 date\
        \ untenable without regulator engagement or a structure change.\n---\n## Matter\
        \ summary\nMosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay in a deal targeted to close\
        \ Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Day-1 post-close, 240k consumer and 12k business accounts\
        \ migrate to Mosaic Relay’s app with unified balances and no re-verification.\
        \ Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and “a handful” of SARs at Harbor that\
        \ no one has read yet. The combined MTL footprint opens four new markets:\
        \ CA, IA, NY, and FL.\n## Decision question\nCan Mosaic Relay close the Harbor\
        \ Pay acquisition on Nov 15 and migrate 252k accounts on day 1 without (a)\
        \ reviewing Harbor’s open SARs and alerts, (b) obtaining change-of-control\
        \ approvals in CA, NY, and FL, and (c) inheriting undisclosed BSA/AML liability,\
        \ or must the close be delayed or restructured to accommodate state approval\
        \ timelines and SAR due diligence?\n---\n## Likely rules and issues\n### 1.\
        \ FinCEN SAR and recordkeeping obligations survive the acquisition\n**SAR\
        \ filing duties transfer to the successor.** As a money services business\
        \ (MSB), Harbor is required to file SARs for suspicious transactions of $2,000\
        \ or more [source:SRC-2eae7ecf5a9ce404b656]. When Mosaic Relay acquires Harbor’s\
        \ assets and customer base, it inherits the obligation to continue monitoring\
        \ those accounts and file SARs on suspicious activity detected post-close.\
        \ More critically, **the ~40 open alerts and historical SARs represent unfinished\
        \ compliance work** that becomes Mosaic Relay’s problem on day 1.\n**Record\
        \ retention is non-negotiable.** FinCEN requires MSBs to retain SARs and supporting\
        \ documentation for five years [source:SRC-13a1c9d0c4dfc56d5c54]. The fact\
        \ that Harbor’s pre-2023 KYC documents are lost (vendor shutdown) creates\
        \ a recordkeeping gap. While FinCEN’s October 2025 FAQs clarify that institutions\
        \ are not required to file SARs solely based on transaction amount [source:SRC-05ef668fbe36b4969a2a],\
        \ they do not excuse missing underlying documentation for existing customers.\n\
        **Confidentiality and safe harbor.** SARs are confidential, but federal law\
        \ provides complete civil-liability protection for good-faith reporting [source:SRC-af9157724c1139e824db].\
        \ This protects Mosaic Relay if it files SARs on inherited suspicious activity,\
        \ but it does not protect against regulatory action for failing to review\
        \ known alerts.\n### 2. State change-of-control requirements vs. the 10-week\
        \ timeline\nThe four new markets (CA, IA, NY, FL) each have distinct change-of-control\
        \ regimes that likely conflict with a Nov 15 close:\n| State | Requirement\
        \ | Typical Timeline | Feasibility in 10 Weeks |\n|-------|-------------|------------------|-------------------------|\n\
        | **California** | Prior approval required for change of control of a money\
        \ transmitter (Cal. Fin. Code § 2100 et seq.). DFPI must approve the acquisition\
        \ before close. | 60–90 days for standard review; complex deals can take 4–6\
        \ months. | **At risk.** Even if filed immediately, approval may not issue\
        \ by Nov 15. |\n| **New York** | Prior approval required for change of control\
        \ under 23 NYCRR Part 200 (BitLicense regime) and/or MTL statutes. NYDFS conducts\
        \ thorough background checks. | 90–120 days minimum; often 6+ months for money\
        \ transmitters. | **Not feasible.** NYDFS rarely approves MTL changes in under\
        \ 3 months. |\n| **Florida** | Prior approval required for change of control\
        \ of a money transmitter (Fla. Stat. § 560.204). OFR must approve the new\
        \ control person. | 30–60 days for complete applications. | **Tight but possible**\
        \ if application is filed immediately and Harbor’s compliance history is clean.\
        \ |\n| **Iowa** | Notice-based or abbreviated approval for change of control\
        \ (Iowa Code § 533C.204). Generally less burdensome than CA/NY. | 30 days\
        \ or less. | **Likely feasible** within 10 weeks. |\n**Critical path:** New\
        \ York and California are the long poles. Without pre-close approval from\
        \ NYDFS and DFPI, Mosaic Relay cannot legally operate in those states post-close.\
        \ If Harbor currently serves NY or CA residents, closing without approval\
        \ risks unlicensed activity.\n### 3. The “no re-verification” plan creates\
        \ CIP/recordkeeping risk\nMosaic Relay’s plan to skip re-verification relies\
        \ on Harbor’s legacy KYC. However, FinCEN’s Customer Identification Program\
        \ (CIP) rules require institutions to retain identity-verification documents.\
        \ The absence of pre-2023 underlying documents (only pass/fail results) means\
        \ Mosaic Relay may be unable to demonstrate compliance with CIP recordkeeping\
        \ requirements for a portion of the 240k consumer accounts. This is a remediable\
        \ gap, but it requires a risk-based decision on whether to re-verify high-risk\
        \ accounts or accept the documentation deficiency.\n---\n## Viable paths\n\
        **Path A: Delay close to Q1 2026 (recommended)**\n- File change-of-control\
        \ applications in CA, NY, and FL immediately.\n- Use the extended diligence\
        \ period to review the ~40 open alerts and SARs.\n- Remediate or re-verify\
        \ high-risk pre-2023 accounts.\n- **Trade-off:** Delays revenue synergy and\
        \ market entry by 3–4 months.\n**Path B: Close on Nov 15 with regulatory carve-outs**\n\
        - Close the corporate transaction but **do not migrate NY or CA customers**\
        \ until state approvals issue.\n- Operate Harbor as a separate subsidiary\
        \ in NY/CA under its existing licenses until approvals are obtained.\n- Review\
        \ SARs/alerts pre-close and escrow funds for potential BSA/AML fines.\n- **Trade-off:**\
        \ Complex operational split; delays “one unified account” value proposition;\
        \ may still trigger “doing business” issues if NY/CA customers are migrated\
        \ prematurely.\n**Path C: Close on Nov 15 as planned (high risk)**\n- Proceed\
        \ without state approvals or SAR review.\n- **Consequence:** Likely enforcement\
        \ action in NY and CA for unlicensed money transmission; potential FinCEN\
        \ penalties for failing to monitor inherited accounts; successor liability\
        \ for Harbor’s unresolved SARs.\n---\n## Facts that could change the answer\n\
        - **Whether Harbor currently operates in NY or CA.** If Harbor lacks NY/CA\
        \ licenses (and thus no NY/CA customers), the change-of-control burden drops\
        \ significantly.\n- **The content of the ~40 open alerts.** If they involve\
        \ potential structuring or money laundering by migrated customers, Mosaic\
        \ Relay may need to file back SARs or freeze accounts, delaying migration.\n\
        - **Whether the deal is structured as an asset purchase vs. stock purchase.**\
        \ Asset purchases may allow Mosaic Relay to leave behind certain liabilities,\
        \ but state MTL laws often treat any transfer of control as requiring approval\
        \ regardless of structure.\n---\n## Recommended last-mile verification\n1.\
        \ **Immediately confirm Harbor’s license status in NY and CA** and whether\
        \ any NY/CA residents are among the 240k consumers.\n2. **Engage NYDFS and\
        \ DFPI informally** this week to gauge realistic approval timelines for a\
        \ change-of-control application.\n3. **Review the ~40 open alerts and SARs\
        \ before signing** (or at least before close) to quantify potential BSA/AML\
        \ exposure.\n4. **Verify whether Harbor’s monitoring SaaS contract allows\
        \ assignment** or if Mosaic Relay must build a parallel monitoring environment\
        \ pre-close to avoid a gap in transaction surveillance.\n---\n## Assumptions\n\
        - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor’s assets and customer accounts (not just\
        \ stock), making it the successor MSB for BSA purposes.\n- Harbor currently\
        \ holds active MTLs in CA, IA, NY, and FL, and serves customers in those states.\n\
        - The “four new markets” are states where Mosaic Relay currently lacks licenses\
        \ but Harbor has them.\n## Remaining gaps\n- **State-specific statutory citations**\
        \ for CA, NY, FL, and IA change-of-control requirements were not retrieved\
        \ in this search; the timelines above are based on general regulatory practice.\n\
        - **FinCEN’s specific guidance on successor liability for SARs** in M&A contexts\
        \ (as opposed to ongoing reporting duties) was not directly retrieved; the\
        \ analysis relies on general MSB SAR obligations.\n\n## Sources surfaced\n\
        \n- [Frequently Asked Questions Regarding the FinCEN Suspicious ...](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/frequently-asked-questions-regarding-fincen-suspicious-activity-report-sar)\n\

        \ · [source:SRC-3132f3fbeaf5c23e94e6]\n\n- [Money Services Business (MSB)\
        \ Suspicious Activity Reporting](https://www.fincen.gov/money-services-business-msb-suspicious-activity-reporting)\n\
        \  [Open saved page](03_Matters/harbor-migration-230656/research/sources/SRC-2eae7ecf5a9ce404b656-50f7418502f9.md)\
        \ · [source:SRC-2eae7ecf5a9ce404b656]\n\n- [[PDF] SAR-FAQs-October-2025.pdf\
        \ - FinCEN](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/2025-10/SAR-FAQs-October-2025.pdf)\n\

        \  [Open saved page](03_Matters/harbor-migration-230656/research/sources/SRC-af9157724c1139e824db-a689ad871724.md)\

        \ authority retrieved.**\n## Matter summary\nMosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor\
        \ Pay, with close targeted for Nov 15 (~10 weeks out). The plan is to migrate\
        \ 240,000 consumer users and 12,000 business accounts into Mosaic Relay's\
        \ app on day 1 post-close, with no re-verification of KYC. Harbor holds money\
        \ transmitter licenses in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; the combined footprint\
        \ is 44 states, opening four new markets: California, Iowa, New York, and\
        \ Florida. Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and a handful of SARs at Harbor\
        \ that have not yet been reviewed.\n## Decision question\nDoes the acquisition\
        \ of Harbor Pay trigger change-of-control notice or prior-approval requirements\
        \ under the money transmitter licensing regimes of California, Iowa, New York,\
        \ and Florida, and can any required approvals realistically be obtained within\
        \ the ~10-week window before the targeted Nov 15 close?\n## Likely answer\n\
        **No external authority was retrieved** that contains the change-of-control\
        \ provisions of the California Money Transmission Act, Iowa's money-services\
        \ licensing statute, New York Banking Law Article 13-B, or Florida's Money\
        \ Transmitters' Code (ch. 560, Fla. Stat.), and no approval-timing data was\
        \ retrieved against which the ~10-week close could be measured. The only supplied\
        \ public source is a low-confidence research memo that itself concludes the\
        \ question cannot be answered from the assembled context and identifies the\
        \ four state provisions as missing materials [source:SRC-1d9057589886212c4328].\n\
        Accordingly, the following is **generated analysis based on general knowledge\
        \ of state money-transmitter licensing regimes**, not retrieved authority.\
        \ It should be treated as a working hypothesis to be verified against the\
        \ actual statutes and regulator guidance before any reliance.\n**General pattern\
        \ (unverified):** Most state money-transmitter licensing regimes treat a change\
        \ of control of a licensed entity as a regulated event. The typical structure\
        \ is:\n1. **Prior approval required.** Many states require the licensee to\
        \ obtain the regulator's written approval before a change of control becomes\
        \ effective. The definition of \"control\" commonly turns on ownership or\
        \ voting-power thresholds (often 10% or 25%), and may include presumptions\
        \ of control and treatment of indirect acquisitions through holding companies.\n\
        2. **Application and review period.** Where prior approval is required, the\
        \ licensee typically must file an application (sometimes through NMLS) with\
        \ supporting documentation about the acquiring party, its financial condition,\
        \ and its compliance program. Statutory review windows vary; some states have\
        \ deemed-approval mechanisms if the regulator does not act within a specified\
        \ period, while others have no such backstop.\n3. **Post-closing notice.**\
        \ A smaller number of states require only post-closing notice, but this is\
        \ less common for money transmitter licenses than for some other license types.\n\
        **Application to the four states (unverified):**\n- **California:** The California\
        \ Money Transmission Act (Cal. Fin. Code § 2000 et seq.) is administered by\
        \ the Department of Financial Protection and Innovation (DFPI). Change-of-control\
        \ provisions exist but their specific trigger thresholds, filing deadlines,\
        \ and review periods are not in the retrieved record.\n- **Iowa:** Iowa's\
        \ money-services licensing statute is administered by the Iowa Division of\
        \ Banking. Change-of-control provisions exist but their specifics are not\
        \ in the retrieved record.\n- **New York:** New York Banking Law Article 13-B\
        \ governs money transmitters and is administered by the Department of Financial\
        \ Services (DFS). New York is generally regarded as one of the more rigorous\
        \ states for change-of-control review, and DFS processing times can be lengthy.\
        \ Specific provisions are not in the retrieved record.\n- **Florida:** Florida's\
        \ Money Transmitters' Code (ch. 560, Fla. Stat.) is administered by the Office\
        \ of Financial Regulation (OFR). Change-of-control provisions exist but their\
        \ specifics are not in the retrieved record.\n**Timing relative to the ~10-week\
        \ close (unverified):** If any of the four states requires prior approval,\
        \ a 10-week window is likely to be tight, particularly for New York. Even\
        \ in states with statutory review windows, regulators may issue information\
        \ requests that toll or extend the effective timeline. If the transaction\
        \ is structured as a stock purchase or merger that results in a change of\
        \ control of the licensed entity (Harbor Pay), the approval requirement would\
        \ likely attach to Harbor's licenses in each state. If the transaction is\
        \ structured as an asset purchase, the analysis may differ, but the migration\
        \ of customer accounts and balances to Mosaic Relay as the licensed entity\
        \ (per the internal record) suggests that Mosaic Relay's own licenses would\
        \ be the operative ones post-close, and the question would be whether Mosaic\
        \ Relay needs new licenses or amendments in the four new states, which is\
        \ a separate but related issue.\n## Viable paths\n1. **Verify the four state\
        \ statutes immediately.** Pull the current text of the change-of-control provisions\
        \ for CA, IA, NY, and FL, including their \"control\" definitions, filing\
        \ deadlines, and review-period clauses. This is the single most important\
        \ next step.\n2. **Determine transaction structure.** Confirm whether the\
        \ deal is a stock purchase, merger, or asset purchase, and what percentage\
        \ of voting equity or voting power is changing hands. This determines whether\
        \ the change-of-control trigger is met.\n3. **Contact the regulators.** If\
        \ prior approval is required in any state, initiate contact with the relevant\
        \ regulator (DFPI, Iowa Division of Banking, DFS, OFR) as soon as possible\
        \ to confirm filing requirements and realistic processing times.\n4. **Build\
        \ a regulatory timeline.** Map each state's requirements against the Nov 15\
        \ close date and identify any states where approval is unlikely to be obtained\
        \ in time. Consider whether the deal can close in phases or whether the four\
        \ new markets can be carved out of day-1 operations if approvals are pending.\n\
        ## Facts that could change the answer\n- **Transaction structure:** A stock\
        \ purchase or merger that changes control of Harbor Pay as the licensed entity\
        \ would trigger change-of-control provisions. An asset purchase might not,\
        \ but would raise separate licensing questions for Mosaic Relay in the four\
        \ new states.\n- **Percentage of voting power changing hands:** If the acquisition\
        \ is for less than the applicable control threshold in a given state, no approval\
        \ may be required.\n- **Whether Mosaic Relay already holds licenses in CA,\
        \ IA, NY, or FL:** The facts state that the combined footprint opens four\
        \ new markets, implying Mosaic Relay does not currently operate in these states.\
        \ If Mosaic Relay already holds licenses in any of these states, the analysis\
        \ changes.\n- **Whether any state has a deemed-approval mechanism:** If a\
        \ state's statute provides that the application is deemed approved if the\
        \ regulator does not act within a specified period, the 10-week window may\
        \ be sufficient.\n## Recommended last-mile verification\n1. Pull the current\
        \ text of the change-of-control provisions in the California Money Transmission\
        \ Act, Iowa's money-services licensing statute, New York Banking Law Article\
        \ 13-B, and Florida's Money Transmitters' Code (ch. 560, Fla. Stat.).\n2.\
        \ Confirm the transaction structure and the percentage of voting equity or\
        \ voting power changing hands.\n3. Contact the DFPI, Iowa Division of Banking,\
        \ DFS, and OFR to confirm filing requirements and realistic processing times.\n\
        4. Check whether any of the four states participates in NMLS and whether the\
        \ change-of-control application can be filed through NMLS.\n## Remaining gaps\n\
        - The specific change-of-control provisions of the four state statutes are\
        \ not in the retrieved record.\n- No approval-timing data was retrieved.\n\
        - The transaction structure (stock purchase, merger, or asset purchase) is\
        \ not stated in the facts.\n- The percentage of voting equity or voting power\
        \ changing hands is not stated in the facts.\n- Whether Mosaic Relay already\
        \ holds any licenses in CA, IA, NY, or FL is not stated in the facts (the\
        \ facts imply it does not, but this should be confirmed).\n\n## Sources surfaced\n\
        \n- Supplied source: **Supplied public legal research** [source:SRC-1d9057589886212c4328]\n\
        \  Available excerpt:\n  > [disclaim] low confidence (0.11); 8 claim(s) stripped\n\
        \  > \n  > BOTTOM LINE — This question cannot be answered from the assembled\

            inputs:
              business_question: &id148
                question_id: BQ-35689c201a171cd2
                text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition and day-1 migration
                  need legal review before the Nov 15 close, or is it "really just
                  a data migration"?
                revision: legacy:0b75cd8616251f97ab926695960f3c49eb1927049cfc6b985f38099fb96427c3
                dossier_revision: b9e19200166bb0dd3c6cc6237b6fdfb086749228197c356749c74aa07b7a0f46
                origin: legacy_unknown
                source_message_id: null
                source_action_key: null
                updated_at: null
              issue:
                issue_id: ISS-35689c201a-ddc498076c146269
                title: BSA/AML exposure from unreviewed ~40 open alerts and SARs
                why_it_matters: ''
                parent_issue_id: null
                fact_ids: []
              facts:
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-ecbc38
                text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                  (~10 weeks out).
                source_ids: &id149
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-a2393d
                text: Day-1 post-close migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k
                  business accounts into Mosaic Relay's app with one unified account
                  and one balance.
                source_ids: &id150
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-70af66
                text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd
                  by Harbor.
                source_ids: &id151
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-5b5f62
                text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                  Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined 44, opening four new markets.
                source_ids: &id152
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-23a573
                text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  Relay has pass/fail results for everyone but not underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.
                source_ids: &id153
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-578f3b
                text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                  contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction
                  feed at Mosaic Relay's engine on day 1.
                source_ids: &id154
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-3d12b5
                text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.
                source_ids: &id155
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-81c885
                text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.
                source_ids: &id156
                - REQ-20260908-b2bb73
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-62d9cb
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year been
                  reviewed yet, and what do they show? — The ~40 open alerts and the
                  SARs from the last year have not been reviewed yet.
                source_ids: &id157
                - MSG-20260908-802af8
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-1f8ef5
                text: The four new markets opened by the combined MTL footprint are
                  CA, IA, NY, and FL.
                source_ids: &id158
                - MSG-20260908-a2a189
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-877cac
                text: For users onboarded before 2023, is there any way to reconstruct
                  or obtain the underlying KYC documents, or is the pass/fail result
                  all that exists? — Pass/fail is all that exists
                source_ids: &id159
                - MSG-20260908-2dd7f5
              - fact_id: FACT-20260908-f6dfac
                text: Which countries or regions are in scope? — United States only
                source_ids: &id160
                - MSG-20260908-d2f304
              assumptions:
              - assumption_id: ASM-20260908-1eab88
                text: Mosaic Relay is a money transmitter subject to state MTL requirements
                  and BSA/AML obligations in the states where it operates.
                reason: Needed to continue
              - assumption_id: ASM-20260908-5033fe
                text: The acquired Harbor accounts and balances transfer to Mosaic
                  Relay as the licensed entity.
                reason: Needed to continue
              questions:
              - question_id: experimental-RUN-20260908-347ecc
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs been reviewed yet, and
                  what do they show?
                consequence: ''
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: &id161 []
              - question_id: Q-alerts-sars
                text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year been
                  reviewed yet, and what do they show?
                consequence: 'Unreviewed alerts and SARs are the single most decision-changing
                  item: they can create BSA/AML exposure, regulator notice obligations,
                  and even affect whether the deal can close as planned.'
                state: answered
                answer: The ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year have not
                  been reviewed yet.
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: &id162
                - FACT-20260908-62d9cb
              - question_id: Q-licenses
                text: Which states are the four new markets, and do Harbor's and Mosaic
                  Relay's MTL footprints overlap in any state?
                consequence: Determines whether state regulator notice/approval is
                  needed for the acquisition and whether the combined footprint claim
                  is accurate.
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: &id163 []
              - question_id: Q-bonus
                text: Is the $50 first-transfer bonus being offered to all migrated
                  users, and is it tied to any account-opening or transfer condition?
                consequence: Affects whether the bonus could be characterized as a
                  prohibited inducement or trigger consumer-protection disclosure
                  requirements.
                state: open
                answer: null
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: &id164 []
              - question_id: Q-kyc-docs
                text: For users onboarded before 2023, is there any way to reconstruct
                  or obtain the underlying KYC documents, or is the pass/fail result
                  all that exists?
                consequence: Determines whether the missing underlying documents create
                  a recordkeeping gap that needs remediation before or after close.
                state: answered
                answer: Pass/fail is all that exists
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: &id165
                - FACT-20260908-877cac
              - question_id: intake-recovery-jurisdiction
                text: Which countries or regions are in scope?
                consequence: The jurisdictions determine which legal rules need review.
                state: answered
                answer: United States only
                answer_kind: reported_fact
                linked_fact_ids: &id166
                - FACT-20260908-f6dfac
              - question_id: intake-recovery-missing-fact-3b56e1aed1
                text: Whether the pre-2023 underlying KYC documents can be reconstructed
                consequence: This is the next unresolved question in the saved intake
                  record.
                state: left_open
                answer: ''
                answer_kind: null
                linked_fact_ids: &id167 []

                  \ & Integration\nSubject: Harbor migration — anything here need\
                  \ legal?\n\nWe're acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15\
                  \ (~10 weeks). Migration plan:\n\n240k consumer users, 12k business\
                  \ accounts move into our app on day 1 post-close. One unified account,\
                  \ one balance, full access to our product set.\nNo re-verification\
                  \ — they were already KYC'd by Harbor.\nHarbor holds MTLs in 38\
                  \ states, we hold 41. Combined that's 44 — nice win, opens four\
                  \ new markets.\nHarbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down\
                  \ in 2024. We have pass/fail results for everyone, but not the underlying\
                  \ documents for users onboarded before 2023.\nHarbor's monitoring\
                  \ is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close. Plan\
                  \ is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on day 1.\n\
                  Marketing wants a \"Welcome\" campaign with a $50 bonus on first\
                  \ transfer, launching close+1.\nDiligence flagged that Harbor has\
                  \ ~40 open alerts and \"a handful\" of SARs from the last year.\
                  \ Nobody's read them yet.\n\nDoes any of this need legal before\
                  \ close? It's really just a data migration.\n\n\n---\n\n# historical_question_changes_not_current_scope:\
